title: Why he wept (Berakhot 28b)
hook: Yochanan ben Zakkai weeps at death, not knowing which road he'll be led on
tomorrow: the same prayer, every day. how does it not go stale?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rabbi Eliezer's first path of life, given from a sickbed: honor your friends. Today, another teacher's last days, and a gentle story about fear.

The students come in quietly, the way people walk into a hospital room. Their teacher, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, is near the end of his life. When he sees them, he begins to cry. They don't know what to do with that. Lamp of Israel, they say. Right-hand pillar. Mighty hammer. Why are you weeping?
screen: `A QUIET ROOM.` → `HE BEGINS TO CRY.` → `LAMP OF ISRAEL, WHY?`

segments.voice: His answer comes in two parts. First: if I were being led before a human king, who is here today and in the grave tomorrow, whose anger doesn't last forever, whom I could calm with words or even bribe with money, even then I would weep. Now I'm being led before the King of kings, who lives forever. Then the part that stops the room. There are two roads before me, he says, one to the Garden of Eden and one to Gehinnom, and I don't know on which one they'll lead me. Shall I not weep? Here's what to tell a friend tonight. The teacher his students called the lamp of Israel didn't pretend to know. He said it in front of them: I don't know, and I'm afraid. The Talmud keeps that in. It doesn't tidy his faith into calm. Then they ask him for a blessing, and he gives a surprising one: may your fear of heaven be like your fear of people. Only that much? they ask. If only, he says. When someone does wrong, they think, just let nobody see me. And at the very end, his words turn toward a guest: prepare a chair for Hezekiah, king of Judah, who is coming.
screen: `BEFORE THE KING OF KINGS.` · `TWO ROADS, AND I DON'T KNOW.` · `FEAR OF HEAVEN, LIKE FEAR OF PEOPLE.` · `A CHAIR FOR HEZEKIAH.` · then, large: `EVEN HE WEPT.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and let one thing you honestly don't know come to mind: about health, someone you love, or what's next. Don't solve it or argue with it. Let it sit beside you, the way the students sat beside their teacher, and breathe with it.
screen: `EYES CLOSED.` · `ONE HONEST UNKNOWN.` · `LET IT SIT BESIDE YOU.`

segments.voice: Why he wept. Yochanan ben Zakkai, near death: two roads before me, and I don't know which. Honest fear, inside a life of faith.
Your line: even he wept. Not knowing, said out loud, by the lamp of Israel. Nineteen of fifty.

howItsDone: Jewish tradition does not ask the dying or the frightened to hide fear; visiting the sick (bikkur cholim) and sitting with them honestly is counted as a mitzvah.

chat.says: saba admitted he's scared about the surgery next week. SABA. he's never scared. what do i say?
options: Don't argue him out of it. Even Yochanan ben Zakkai wept and said, I don't know.
Remind him real faith means never being scared, so he should feel fine.
Change the subject fast; saying fear out loud only makes it grow bigger.
chat.meaning: The lamp of Israel wept and named what he didn't know. In this story honest fear sits inside faith; you can sit with Saba in it.

Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.meaning: a sage his students called the lamp of Israel

Gehinnom.meaning: in rabbinic teaching, a place of judgment after death
